questions.html: In which of the following addition problems (using two's complement notation) does an overflow error occur?
questions.solution:
Answer: D

Source solution 1 (score: 3)

Given using 2's complement notation 

A. 1100 + 1100 = 1000

     Overflow => 0. 0. 1 + 1. 1. 0 = 0

B. 1100 + 0100 = 0000

     Overflow => 0. 1. 0 + 1. 0. 1 = 0

C. 0011 + 1010 = 1101

     Overflow => 1. 0. 1 + 0. 1. 0 = 0

D. 0100 + 0100 = 1000

     Overflow => 1. 1. 1 + 0. 0. 0 = 1

Answer: D 

Source solution 2 (score: 0)

option A: 1100 + 1100  => (-4) +(-4) = -8 which we get correctly as 1000 with 1 as end carry discard.
option B : 1100 +0100 => opposite signs can never cause overflow
option C: 0011 +1010 => opposite signs can never cause overflow.
option D: 0100 +0100 => 4 +4 = 8 but we get answer as 1000 which in 2's complement is -8. This  error happened because of overflow
Hence option D is the answer

questions.html: Perform the following arithmetic operations on $8$-bit $2's$ complement values. Express your answer using $8$-bit $2's$ complement. Which of the following operations results in an overflow?
questions.solution:
Answer: B, D

Source solution 1 (score: 4)

A) 0010 0001 + 0001 1111 = 0100 0000

     Overflow => 1. 1. 0 + 0. 0. 1 = 0 

B) 0110 1100 + 0101 1101 = 1100 1001

     Overflow => 1. 1. 1 + 0. 0. 0 = 1

C) 1100 1100 - 0010 0101 = 1100 1100 + (2's complement of 0010 0101) 

                                               = 1100 1100 + 1101 1011 

                                               = 1010 0111

     Overflow => 0. 0. 1 + 1. 1. 0 = 0 

D) 1000 1111 - 0101 0101 = 1000 1111 + (2's complement of 0101 0101) 

                                               = 1000 1111 + 1010 1011

                                               = 0011 1010

     Overflow => 0. 0. 0 + 1. 1. 1 = 1

Answer : B,D

 

Source solution 2 (score: 1)

Overflow in 2’s complement addition occurs when adding two numbers of the same sign gives a result with the opposite sign.

  • If both numbers are positive (MSB = 0) but the result is negative (MSB = 1).

  • If both numbers are negative (MSB = 1) but the result is positive (MSB = 0).

Answer: B and D

questions.html: Which of the following decimal numbers can be exactly represented in binary notation with a finite number of bits ?
questions.solution:
Answer: D

Source solution 1 (score: 4)

1. The Golden Rule: Powers of 2

Koi bhi decimal fraction ($0.x$) binary mein tabhi terminate (khatam) hoga jab uske denominator (simplest form mein) ke factors sirf 2 ki powers ($2^n$) honge.

Agar denominator mein 2 ke alawa koi aur prime factor (jaise 3, 5, 7) aa gaya, toh woh binary mein infinite/recurring ho jayega.

Method 2: 

Aap ise multiply karke bhi check kar sakte hain. Agar multiply karte-karte fractional part $0.0$ ho jaye, toh woh finite hai.

Tricks 

  • $1/2, 1/4, 1/8, 1/16, 3/8, 7/32 \dots$ $\rightarrow$ Finite (Kyunki denominator $2^n$ hai).

  • $1/3, 1/5, 1/10, 1/6 \dots$ $\rightarrow$ Infinite (Kyunki denominator mein $2$ ke alawa kuch aur hai). 

  • so option D is correct. 

Source solution 2 (score: 1)

A , B ,C will lead to non terminating and repeating bits.
